title: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral Program: $40,000 Per Year for PhD Research in Canada
summary: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D) Program provides substantial financial support to outstanding doctoral students conducting research in health, natural sciences and engineering, social sciences and humanities. The scholarship is jointly administered through Canada’s three federal research agencies: the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR), the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC), and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC). Successful scholars receive $40,000 per year for three years , allowing them to devote greater attention to doctoral research, work with leading research mentors and contribute to Canada’s research and innovation ecosystem. The program also supports interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary research and includes priority research areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, health, climate resilience, food and water security, democratic and community resilience, advanced manufacturing, and defence-related technologies. Opportunity Details Opportunity: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D) Category: Scholarship Study level: Doctoral / PhD Funding: $40,000 per year Duration: 36 months Application deadline: October 17, 2026, for applicants applying directly to an agency Institutional deadline: Varies by Canadian institution and may be significantly earlier Fields: Health, natural sciences, engineering, social sciences and humanities Eligible applicants: Canadian and eligible international doctoral students Study location: Eligible Canadian institutions and, under specific conditions, eligible degree-granting institutions outside Canada Administered by: CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC About the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral Program The CGRS D is part of Canada s Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS) . The broader suite includes: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master’s (CGRS M) Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D) Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA) The CGRS D is designed to recognize and support outstanding doctoral researchers and help develop the next generation of highly qualified innovators, knowledge workers and creative thinkers. The scholarship provides recipients with financial support that can enable them to concentrate more fully on their doctoral studies and research activities. It also provides flexibility for scholars to seek strong research mentors and participate in Canada s research ecosystem. The program covers a broad range of academic disciplines, including research in: Health Natural sciences Engineering Social sciences Humanities Interdisciplinary research Multidisciplinary research Scholarship Value and Duration Successful CGRS D recipients receive: $40,000 per year for 36 months. This represents a total potential scholarship value of: $120,000 over three years. The funding is intended to support doctoral students while they undertake eligible research-oriented doctoral studies. The financial support can allow recipients to dedicate more time to their research, develop their research skills, work with appropriate research mentors and contribute to research activities during and after the scholarship period. Who Can Apply? The CGRS D is intended for outstanding doctoral students who are undertaking eligible research-oriented doctoral programs. Applicants must satisfy the program s eligibility requirements, including requirements relating to their doctoral study progress and registration status. Doctoral Study Requirement By December 31 of the calendar year of application , applicants must have completed no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent study in the doctoral program for which they are requesting funding. The calculation includes the applicable doctoral studies regardless of whether those studies were completed at the same institution or within the same program. The agencies count: All months of full-time study, including summer months Two terms of part-time study as one term of full-time study Previous doctoral study toward the same degree, even if completed at another institution or in another program Fast-Track Programs For applicants who transferred from a master s program into a doctoral program through a fast-track arrangement, the months of study are calculated beginning from the date of transfer into the doctoral program. Joint Programs For joint programs such as: MA/PhD MSc/PhD MBA/PhD the calculation begins from the date the applicant officially registered in either portion of the joint program, including the master s portion. Joint Professional Undergraduate/PhD Programs For programs such as: MD/PhD JD/PhD DVM/PhD only the months completed in the PhD portion are counted. Requirements for the Doctoral Program The doctoral program must be predominantly research-oriented. It must lead to a substantial research or scholarly requirement such as: A thesis A dissertation A major research project Scholarly publication Performance Recital Exhibit The research or scholarly work must be subject to merit review by a panel of experts at the institution as part of the requirements for completing the program. Certain joint professional doctoral programs can also qualify when they contain a significant autonomous research component. This includes eligible joint programs involving professional degrees such as: MD/PhD DVM/PhD JD/PhD MBA/PhD Clinically oriented programs can also qualify when they meet the program s research requirements. Clinical psychology is specifically mentioned as an example. International Applicants International students can apply, but specific conditions apply. If you are not a Canadian citizen, permanent resident of Canada or protected person under Canada s Immigration and Refugee Protection Act , you must be registered in your doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline . The program states that up to 15% of awards will be available to international applicants . This is particularly important for international students considering the opportunity from outside Canada: simply being an international student is not enough. The applicant must meet the doctoral registration requirement at an eligible Canadian institution by the relevant deadline. Can the Scholarship Be Held Outside Canada? The CGRS D may be held at an eligible Canadian institution or, under certain conditions, at a degree-granting institution outside Canada. However, holding the scholarship outside Canada is subject to additional eligibility requirements. To hold the award at an eligible degree-granting institution outside Canada, an applicant must: Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident of Canada or protected person as of the application deadline; and Have completed at least one previous undergraduate or graduate degree at a Canadian institution. The program indicates that up to 20% of all doctoral awards may be available to be held outside Canada . Therefore, the rules for holding the award outside Canada are different from the rules governing international applicants who are studying in Canada. Important Application Restrictions Applicants should carefully review the restrictions before applying. One CRTAS Application Per Academic Year Applicants can apply to only one CRTAS program per academic year through CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC. If an applicant submits applications to more than one program, only the first eligible application submitted to the agencies will be retained. Maximum of Three CGRS D Applications An individual can apply to the CGRS D program a maximum of three times . Previous Doctoral Scholarships Applicants cannot have already received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC. This includes the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship . Tenure or Tenure-Track Positions Additional restrictions apply to applicants who hold tenure or tenure-track appointments. Recipients of CIHR or NSERC awards cannot simultaneously hold a tenure or tenure-track appointment or be on leave from such an appointment during their CGRS D award. SSHRC has different provisions for approved leave from a tenure or tenure-track position when undertaking a first doctoral degree. Applicants who are uncertain about their eligibility should contact the relevant agency. Priority Research Areas The Government of Canada has identified several priority research areas that may receive additional award offers for meritorious applications aligned with these areas. These include: 1. Advanced Digital Technologies Research may include areas such as: Artificial intelligence Quantum technologies Cybersecurity Other advanced digital technologies 2. Health and Biotechnology This includes research connected to: Health Biotechnology Related scientific and medical research areas 3. Clean Technology and Resource Value Chains Research addressing clean technologies and sustainable resource-related systems may align with this priority. 4. Environment, Climate Resilience and the Arctic Research related to environmental challenges, climate resilience and Arctic issues is included among the priority areas. 5. Food and Water Security Research addressing food systems, water security and related global challenges may align with this area. 6. Democratic and Community Resilience Research examining issues related to democratic systems and community resilience is another identified priority. 7. Manufacturing and Advanced Materials This includes research involving advanced manufacturing and materials science. 8. Defence and Dual-Use Technologies Research related to defence and technologies with potential civilian and defence applications is also included. Applicants whose research aligns with a priority area should consult the relevant agency s application instructions for guidance on identifying that alignment. Additional Funding Opportunities CGRS D recipients may also be eligible for supplementary funding. The three agencies may offer joint initiatives and supplements in collaboration with organizations from: The public sector Private sector Not-for-profit sector These initiatives can support research training, networking and other activities connected with the strategic objectives of the participating organizations. Additional funding opportunities may vary by agency and competition. Support for Indigenous Student Researchers The program includes specific measures supporting Indigenous student researchers and Indigenous research. The Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative can provide additional support to eligible Indigenous students whose nations or communities are located in Canada. Successful eligible CGRS D applicants may receive an Indigenous Scholars Supplement valued at $5,000 for one year , subject to available funding and the relevant conditions. The program also includes measures designed to support Indigenous research and respectful relationships with Indigenous Peoples and communities. These measures include provisions concerning: Indigenous research Self-identified Indigenous doctoral applicants Research review Special circumstances affecting academic or career paths Indigenous representation and expertise on review committees Additional Support for Black Student Researchers The Government of Canada has also provided additional funding intended to increase direct support for Black student researchers. Meritorious CGRS D applicants who self-identify as Black and consent to being considered for designated funding may be selected for this additional support. Each of the three agencies may have up to 10 additional awards reserved for Black student researchers . These opportunities are subject to the program s eligibility, selection and funding conditions. How to Apply Applicants must apply through the agency that is best aligned with the subject matter of their proposed research. The three relevant agencies are: CIHR – Canadian Institutes of Health Research NSERC – Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada SSHRC – Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council Selecting the correct agency is important because applications are reviewed by experts whose disciplinary expertise should correspond to the applicant s field of research. CIHR Applicants Applicants applying through CIHR should use the ResearchNET platform and follow CIHR s specific application instructions. NSERC Applicants Applicants applying through NSERC should use NSERC s online application system and follow the CGRS D application instructions. SSHRC Applicants Applicants applying through SSHRC should use the SSHRC registration and application system and follow the agency s specific doctoral scholarship instructions. Applicants who are uncertain about which agency is appropriate should review the federal guidance on selecting the appropriate granting agency or contact the relevant agency. Where Should Applicants Submit Their Applications? The correct application channel depends on the applicant s registration status and, in some cases, whether the institution has a doctoral award quota. Submitting through the wrong channel can result in rejection. International Applicants International applicants have specific submission rules. An international applicant who is currently registered in a doctoral program at a Canadian institution with a doctoral award quota for the relevant agency generally applies through that Canadian institution. An international applicant who is registered in a doctoral program at a Canadian institution without a doctoral award quota for the selected agency applies directly to the appropriate agency. Applicants on an approved leave of absence from an institution are considered to remain registered at that institution for these purposes. Canadian Applicants For Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons, the submission route depends on their registration status during the calendar year of application and the institution involved. Depending on the circumstances, an applicant may need to apply: Through their current Canadian institution Through a Canadian institution where they were registered during the year Directly to the relevant federal agency Applicants should carefully review the official submission tables and confirm their status with their faculty of graduate studies or equivalent office where necessary. Understanding Institutional Quotas A quota refers to the maximum number of applications that a Canadian institution can forward to a particular federal research agency. Institutions have separate quotas for: CIHR NSERC SSHRC If an applicant must apply through an institution, they should contact the relevant graduate studies office to determine: Whether the institution has a quota Which agency s quota applies The institution s internal deadline Any internal selection process Required institutional documents Application Deadline October 17, 2026 Applicants who are eligible to apply directly to an agency must submit their application before 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 17, 2026 . If the deadline falls on a weekend, applications can be submitted on the following business day before 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Applicants should not wait until the final hours because the agencies warn that high traffic on online application systems can cause delays. Institutional Deadlines Applicants applying through a Canadian institution must follow the institution s own deadline. The institutional deadline can be significantly earlier than October 17 . Therefore, applicants should contact their university s faculty of graduate studies as early as possible rather than relying solely on the federal agency deadline. Late applications are not accepted. What Happens After Submission? Applications undergo an evaluation process. Institutional Review Where applications are submitted through a Canadian institution, the institution s faculty of graduate studies or equivalent body coordinates an institutional evaluation. The institution then forwards applications according to its available agency quota. Agency Review Applications submitted directly to an agency, as well as applications forwarded by Canadian institutions, are evaluated by agency-specific review committees. The reviewers assess the applications according to the CGRS D selection criteria. How Applications Are Evaluated The CGRS D uses two major selection criteria. 1. Research Potential – 50% Research potential accounts for 50% of the assessment. Reviewers consider factors including: Quality of the research proposal Specificity and focus of the research question or objectives Feasibility of the proposed research Quality of the methodology Significance of the proposed research Expected contribution to the relevant research field Potential to successfully conduct the proposed research Publications and other research outputs Reports Posters Abstracts Presentations Patents Scholarly and creative outputs Knowledge translation activities Community products Critical thinking Sound judgment Originality Initiative Autonomy Community involvement Outreach Responsible and ethical research conduct Ability to communicate research concepts clearly Overall quality and presentation of the application Where relevant, applicants can also demonstrate how equity, diversity and inclusion considerations are integrated into their research. 2. Relevant Experience and Achievements – 50% The second half of the assessment focuses on relevant experience and achievements obtained both inside and outside academia. This criterion accounts for another 50% . Relevant factors can include: Academic training Relevant professional training Lived experience Traditional teachings Scholarships Awards Academic distinctions Academic record Transcripts Duration of previous studies Courses completed Course load Relative academic standing where available Professional activities Academic activities Extracurricular activities Collaboration with supervisors Collaboration with colleagues and peers Teaching Mentoring Supervision Coaching Project management Science or research promotion Community outreach Volunteer work Civic engagement Committee leadership Conference organization Meeting organization Participation in academic or professional organizations, associations and clubs This means the application is not assessed solely on the proposed research project. The applicant s broader academic, professional and extracurricular record is also considered. Notification of Results Applicants will be notified of the results by: April 30. Successful award holders who accept the scholarship may have their names and basic award information published on the relevant agency s website. The agencies publication of award information is subject to applicable Canadian privacy and access-to-information legislation. Official Language of the Application Applicants can submit their application in either of Canada s two official languages: English French If supporting documents are written in a language other than English or French, applicants must provide a certified translation. Canadian institutions must have mechanisms for reviewing applications in the official language in which they are submitted. Career Development and Individual Development Plans The agencies encourage applicants and award holders to actively plan their careers during their research training. Individual Development Plans, or IDPs, can help doctoral researchers: Identify career objectives Identify skills gaps Develop professional skills Plan career development Reflect on strengths and values Prepare for future employment and research opportunities However, the program explicitly states that IDPs are not a selection or evaluation criterion for the CGRS D . Research Security and International Research Applicants and award holders undertaking research activities outside Canada are encouraged to consult Canadian government resources concerning travel and research security. Relevant resources include: Travel advice and advisories Travel health notices Registration of Canadians abroad Emergency assistance outside Canada Safeguarding Your Research Research security training resources Guidance concerning research organizations and sensitive technologies The program also notes that the Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern (STRAC Policy) does not apply to scholarship and fellowship programs such as the Canada Research Training Awards Suite . Nevertheless, Canadian researchers are encouraged to follow applicable research-security guidance and exercise due diligence when conducting research activities. Important Things Applicants Should Know Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully verify the following: Whether they are eligible for the CGRS D. How many months of doctoral study they will have completed by December 31. Whether they have previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC. Whether they have already applied to another CRTAS program during the academic year. Whether they have previously applied to the CGRS D and how many applications they have made. Which federal agency best matches their research subject. Whether their Canadian institution has an applicable doctoral award quota. Whether they need to submit through their institution or directly to the agency. Their institution s internal deadline. Whether their doctoral program meets the research-oriented program requirements. Whether they meet the special registration requirements applicable to international applicants. Whether all required supporting documents and reference letters will be submitted on time. Applicants should also avoid waiting until the final day because online application systems may experience heavy traffic near the deadline. Category of the Opportunity Scholarship This is a doctoral research scholarship under Canada s Canada Research Training Awards Suite. Who Qualifies for This Opportunity? The opportunity is primarily for: Current doctoral/PhD students Students in eligible research-oriented doctoral programs Applicants conducting research in eligible fields Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons who meet the program requirements Eligible international doctoral students who are registered at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline Applicants who have completed no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study by December 31 of the application year Academic Qualifications Applicants must be enrolled in an eligible doctoral program that is predominantly research-oriented and includes an appropriate thesis, dissertation, major research project or equivalent scholarly requirement. Eligible Fields Research may fall within: Health Natural sciences Engineering Social sciences Humanities Interdisciplinary research Multidisciplinary research Countries and Regions The program is administered by the Government of Canada and is open to eligible applicants internationally, but international applicants face specific Canadian doctoral-registration requirements. For international applicants, the key requirement is that they must be registered in an eligible doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline. Therefore, applicants from Ghana, other African countries, Asia, Europe, the Americas, Oceania and other regions may potentially qualify as international applicants if they satisfy the applicable requirements and are registered in an eligible Canadian doctoral program. Eligibility is not determined simply by nationality or continent. Applicants must satisfy the program s academic, doctoral-study, registration and other eligibility requirements. Application Link Applicants should use the application platform corresponding to their research agency: CIHR: ResearchNET NSERC: NSERC Online Services SSHRC: SSHRC registration and application system Applicants should first determine which agency best matches their research subject before starting the application. Official Website For the full eligibility requirements, application instructions, agency-specific guidance, deadlines and official updates, visit the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) official CGRS D funding opportunity page. For more scholarships visit the OFY Website HERE Conclusion The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Doctoral (CGRS D) is a major Canadian doctoral research funding program providing $40,000 annually for up to 36 months , for a potential total of $120,000 . The scholarship covers a broad range of research areas across health, natural sciences, engineering, social sciences and humanities. It also identifies priority areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, quantum technologies, biotechnology, climate resilience, food and water security, democratic and community resilience, advanced manufacturing, and defence and dual-use technologies. International students can be considered, but they must pay particular attention to the requirement to be registered in an eligible Canadian doctoral program by the application deadline. Applicants applying directly to an agency must submit their applications by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 17, 2026 , while applicants applying through Canadian institutions must follow their institution s earlier internal deadline where applicable. Because the scholarship evaluates both research potential and relevant experience and achievements , prospective applicants should prepare a strong research proposal while also presenting a comprehensive record of their academic, professional, research, leadership, community and extracurricular achievements. title: METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme Cohort 2 2026 | Apply to Build and Scale Your AI Solution
summary: Applications are now open for Cohort 2 of the METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme, an opportunity designed to support innovators developing early-stage artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-enabled solutions. The programme is seeking individuals and teams with promising AI ideas who are ready to move beyond the idea stage, strengthen their technical capabilities, develop their solutions and explore pathways towards bringing their products to market. Following the first cohort, timbuktoo UniPods is opening a new opportunity for innovators who are building real AI solutions and are looking for structured technical, entrepreneurial and mentorship support. One of the distinctive features of the programme is that applicants do not need to prepare pitch decks as part of the application. Instead, the programme is focused on innovators with real ideas, real code and the motivation to build. Applications for Cohort 2 are open until 30 October 2026. What Is the METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme? The METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme is an innovation and capacity-building programme aimed at supporting early-stage innovators working on artificial intelligence and AI-enabled solutions. The programme brings together technical learning, entrepreneurship development, mentorship and access to a wider innovation network. Through these components, selected innovators can strengthen both the technology behind their solutions and their understanding of how to develop them into viable products. The programme is particularly relevant for innovators who already have an early-stage AI solution or are actively developing an AI-enabled product and want additional support to take it further. Who Is the Programme Looking For? Cohort 2 is looking for innovators developing early-stage AI and AI-enabled solutions. Applications can be submitted by: Individual innovators Teams of innovators Developers and technical builders working on AI solutions Innovators developing AI-enabled products Early-stage founders and builders seeking to advance their solutions Applicants should have a genuine interest in building and improving an AI or AI-enabled solution. The programme places emphasis on actual development rather than presentation alone. Applicants therefore do not need a pitch deck to demonstrate their interest. The focus is on real ideas, real code and the willingness to build. Female innovators are especially encouraged to apply. What Will Selected Innovators Receive? Selected participants will have access to several forms of technical, entrepreneurial and mentorship support. 1. AI Course from MIT Participants will have access to an AI course from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). This component is intended to strengthen participants understanding of artificial intelligence and provide additional learning that can support the development of their solutions. 2. AI Technical Skilling Selected innovators will receive AI technical skilling designed to help them strengthen their technical capabilities. For innovators who are already building AI or AI-enabled products, technical development can be important for improving their solutions, addressing technical challenges and advancing their projects. 3. Entrepreneurship Programme Participants will also gain access to Wadhwani s 14-week entrepreneurship programme. The programme covers important areas of entrepreneurship and product development, including: Customer discovery Business modelling Taking products to market Investment readiness This provides innovators with an opportunity to develop not only their technology but also the business and market understanding required to take a solution beyond the development stage. 4. Technical Mentorship Participants will have access to technical mentors who can provide guidance as they work on their AI solutions. Mentorship can be particularly useful for innovators who are facing technical challenges or need additional guidance while developing and refining their products. 5. Access to the timbuktoo Network Selected innovators will also gain access to the wider timbuktoo network. Being part of a broader innovation network can provide opportunities for participants to connect with other innovators, ecosystem stakeholders and individuals working across the technology and entrepreneurship space. 6. Opportunity to Attend an In-Person Bootcamp in Addis Ababa Participants may also have the chance to join an in-person bootcamp in Addis Ababa. The bootcamp can provide an opportunity for selected innovators to engage directly with other participants, mentors and programme stakeholders while working on their solutions in a collaborative environment. No Pitch Decks Needed One of the notable aspects of the Cohort 2 application is that applicants do not need pitch decks. The programme is looking for innovators who are actively building and experimenting with their ideas. Rather than focusing only on presentations, applicants are encouraged to demonstrate their ability and commitment through their actual work, ideas and code. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to technical builders who have begun developing a solution and want structured support to move it forward. Why This Programme Matters for AI Innovators Developing an AI solution requires more than having an innovative idea. Builders often need technical knowledge, customer feedback, business development skills, mentorship and an understanding of how to take a product to market. The METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme brings several of these elements together within one programme. Participants can therefore work on different aspects of their development journey, including: Improving their AI knowledge and technical capabilities Developing and refining their existing solutions Understanding their potential customers and users Exploring appropriate business models Learning how to take their products to market Preparing their ventures for investment Receiving technical mentorship Connecting with the wider innovation ecosystem Who Should Consider Applying? The programme may be particularly relevant to innovators who: Are developing an early-stage AI solution Are building an AI-enabled product Have started writing code for an AI-related solution Are looking for technical support to advance an existing project Want to strengthen their entrepreneurship and business development skills Need guidance on customer discovery and business modelling Want to understand how to take their product to market Are interested in becoming investment-ready Want to connect with mentors and other innovators Are interested in participating in the wider timbuktoo innovation ecosystem Female innovators are especially encouraged to apply. How the Programme Can Support Your Innovation Journey The programme combines several stages of innovation development. At the technical level, participants can strengthen their AI skills and work with technical mentors. At the product level, the entrepreneurship component can help innovators better understand their customers and develop appropriate business models. At the market level, participants can learn about taking products to market and preparing their ventures for investment. This combination can help innovators approach their projects from both a technical and entrepreneurial perspective. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for Cohort 2 of the METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme is: 30 October 2026 Applicants should complete and submit their applications before the deadline. How to Apply Interested innovators should apply through the official application process for the METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme. Applicants should ensure that the information they provide accurately represents their AI or AI-enabled solution and their development work. Since the programme is focused on real ideas and real code, applicants should clearly demonstrate what they are building and why they are interested in taking the solution further. Application Deadline: 30 October 2026 Conclusion The METI UniPods AI Innovation Programme Cohort 2 provides an opportunity for early-stage AI and AI-enabled solution builders to strengthen their technical and entrepreneurial capabilities. Selected innovators can gain access to an AI course from MIT, AI technical skilling, technical mentors, Wadhwani s 14-week entrepreneurship programme and the wider timbuktoo network. Participants may also have the opportunity to attend an in-person bootcamp in Addis Ababa. With applications open to both individuals and teams, and no pitch deck required, the programme is designed for innovators who are ready to demonstrate their ideas through real building and development. Innovators developing early-stage AI or AI-enabled solutions are encouraged to review the application requirements and submit their applications before 30 October 2026 . title: Michael D. Eisner Arts & Culture Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded Two-Year Leadership Opportunity for Global Arts and Culture Leaders
summary: The Michael D. Eisner Arts Culture Fellowship is a two-year leadership program for accomplished arts and culture leaders from around the world who are ready to expand their influence and use their creative platforms to contribute to society. The fellowship is a partnership between the Aspen Global Leadership Network and the Aspen Institute Arts Program , with support from the Eisner Foundation . The program brings together leaders working across the global arts ecosystem, including artists, filmmakers, performers, writers, producers, cultural executives, curators, financiers, and other professionals who help create, support, distribute, or shape cultural work. Fellows participate in four immersive seminars over approximately two years, engage in moderated dialogue with peers, explore questions of leadership and social impact, and develop an impact journey connected to the challenges they want to address. For Class 2 , nominations are currently open, with submissions accepted through November 3, 2026 . Importantly, this is a nomination-based opportunity rather than a self-application program : interested candidates must identify a third-party nominator who can put them forward. What Is the Michael D. Eisner Arts Culture Fellowship? The Michael D. Eisner Arts Culture Fellowship was created to support arts and cultural leaders who have already achieved meaningful success in their respective fields and are reaching a point where they want to translate that success into broader societal impact. Rather than focusing only on artistic achievement or professional advancement, the fellowship asks participants to consider a broader leadership question: How can people working in the arts use their creativity, platforms, networks, and leadership abilities to contribute to a better future? According to the Aspen Institute, the fellowship is designed for global arts leaders who are ready to move from success in their fields toward significant impact. It recognizes that arts and culture can influence how societies understand themselves, imagine their futures, communicate ideas, and respond to major social challenges. The fellowship brings together an intergenerational group of approximately 20–22 leaders for the second class. Participants come from different areas of the arts and cultural ecosystem, allowing the program to create a multidisciplinary environment where creative professionals can learn from people working in different fields and generations. Who Is the Fellowship Designed For? The Michael D. Eisner Arts Culture Fellowship is intended for accomplished arts and culture leaders who have demonstrated significant success in their careers and are ready to explore how their leadership and creativity can contribute to addressing wider societal challenges. The Aspen Institute describes three broad groups of leaders the fellowship seeks to bring together. 1. Leaders Who Make Art This group includes people directly involved in creating artistic work, such as: Artists Performers Writers Designers Painters Dancers Architects Other creative practitioners These individuals use their creative practices to tell stories, explore ideas, challenge assumptions, preserve culture, and influence how people understand the world. 2. Leaders Who Create the Conditions for Art The fellowship also recognizes people who may not personally create the final artistic work but play an important role in making artistic production possible. This can include: Producers Agents Financiers Curators Academics Artist residency directors Cultural managers Other arts-support professionals These professionals help provide the resources, structures, opportunities, institutions, and environments that allow artists and cultural practitioners to develop and share their work. 3. Leaders Who Bring Art to the World The third group consists of professionals who help determine how art reaches audiences and how cultural ideas circulate through society. Examples include: Studio executives Gallery owners Museum directors and curators Magazine editors Film festival executives Media executives Cultural commentators Philanthropists Other cultural leaders who build audiences and shape public discourse The Aspen Institute says candidates should demonstrate boldness, vision, and the capacity to influence others through their work . The program also aims to create a diverse, intergenerational, and global cohort representing different disciplines, experiences, and perspectives. What Does the Fellowship Offer? The fellowship is structured as a two-year leadership experience consisting of four major seminars. Across the program, Fellows participate in approximately 25 days of programming distributed across the four seminars. Each seminar is an immersive, approximately week-long experience designed around reflection, peer exchange, dialogue, and leadership development. The seminars use the Aspen Institute s text-based dialogue approach. Rather than functioning as a conventional lecture or classroom program, the experience encourages Fellows to engage deeply with ideas, readings, other participants, and questions about their own leadership. Participants explore issues including: Leadership and personal values The responsibilities that accompany influence The role of arts and culture in society How creative leaders can contribute to social change Different perspectives on major global challenges How leaders can translate their values into action How creative platforms can be used for meaningful impact The fellowship therefore goes beyond professional networking. It is structured around reflection and dialogue intended to help participants examine their leadership roles and determine how they can apply their influence to broader challenges. Fellowship Seminar Schedule Candidates for Class 2 must be able to attend all four seminars in full. The current seminar schedule published by the Aspen Institute is: Seminar 1: September 26–October 1, 2027 Seminar 2: June 4–10, 2028 Seminar 3: February 25–March 2, 2029, or March 11–16, 2029 Seminar 4: September 16–21, 2029 The third seminar offers participants a choice between two dates associated with Leading in a Global Context seminars in different locations. Because full participation is an important part of the fellowship experience, candidates who cannot commit to attending all four seminars are not considered for the current class. Where Will the Fellowship Take Place? The fellowship experience includes seminars at the Aspen Meadows campus in Colorado , as well as other cultural hubs. This means Fellows should be prepared for an international, in-person leadership experience involving travel to seminar locations. The program is intentionally designed to bring participants together physically for extended periods of dialogue, reflection, collaboration, and peer learning. Is the Michael D. Eisner Arts Culture Fellowship Fully Funded? Yes. Participation in the fellowship is provided at no cost to Fellows or their organizations . The Eisner Foundation funds the program, covering: Seminar tuition Program materials Lodging Fellows are responsible for their travel to and from seminar locations and incidental expenses . The Aspen Institute also notes that limited assistance may be available to help offset travel costs in special circumstances. Therefore, although this is often described as a fully funded fellowship, applicants should understand the distinction between the costs covered by the program and expenses that remain the responsibility of Fellows. What Happens After Completing the Fellowship? One of the significant long-term components of the program is membership in the Aspen Global Leadership Network (AGLN) . Upon completing the Michael D. Eisner Arts Culture Fellowship, Fellows become lifelong members of the AGLN. The Aspen Institute describes the network as a global community of more than 4,200 leaders across more than 60 countries. Membership can provide an opportunity to remain connected to other leaders across sectors and geographical regions after the fellowship itself has ended. The network includes leaders working in areas such as: Arts and culture Business Technology Public service Health Other professional and social-impact fields The fellowship therefore extends beyond the two-year program itself, with participants becoming part of a broader leadership community. What Kind of Leaders Is the Aspen Institute Looking For? The program is not simply looking for people who have worked in the arts. It is looking for people who have demonstrated significant success and leadership and who are prepared to think about how their influence can be used more broadly. According to the current nomination information, strong candidates should demonstrate: Significant professional achievement Leadership experience Boldness Vision The ability to influence others A desire to broaden their impact A willingness to engage deeply with other leaders A commitment to addressing major societal challenges The ability to participate fully in the two-year fellowship experience The program is also intentionally designed to create a cohort with different generations, disciplines, experiences, and perspectives. How Does the Nomination Process Work? A particularly important detail for prospective candidates is that the Michael D. Eisner Arts Culture Fellowship does not accept self-nominations . title: Young CAS Grant 2027–2029 in Norway: NOK 750,000 Research Grant for Early-Career Researchers — Applications Open
summary: The Centre for Advanced Study (CAS) at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters has opened applications for the Young CAS Grant for August 2027 to June 2029 , offering an opportunity for young researchers to establish and lead an international research project while developing their research leadership experience and professional network. The programme is designed around residential, collaborative research rather than a conventional individual fellowship. Successful applicants become the Principal Investigator (PI) of a Young CAS project and assemble an international team of researchers around a research question that fits CAS s focus on excellent, fundamental and curiosity-driven research. For the 2027–2029 programme, CAS will select two Young CAS projects . Each selected project can receive up to NOK 750,000 over two years , alongside office facilities, accommodation support and administrative assistance connected with the programme. Application deadline: 19 November 2026 Young CAS Grant 2027–2029 at a Glance The Young CAS Grant is intended for early-career researchers who have completed a PhD and are building their research careers. Key details include: Opportunity: Young CAS Grant Host institution: Centre for Advanced Study (CAS), The Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters Location: Oslo, Norway Programme period: August 2027 to June 2029 Number of projects selected: Two Funding: Up to NOK 750,000 per project over two years Research model: Collaborative and residential research Research disciplines: Researchers from all disciplines are encouraged to apply Research leadership: The applicant serves as Principal Investigator Application system: UNIFOR electronic application system Application language: English Application format: Required documents must be submitted as PDF files Application deadline: 19 November 2026 at 23:59 Selection decision: February 2027 What Is the Young CAS Grant? The Young CAS Grant is a collaborative initiative involving the Centre for Advanced Study (CAS) and the Young Academy of Norway (AYF) , with support from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters (DNVA) . Rather than simply providing an individual researcher with funding, the programme gives the successful applicant an opportunity to design, organise and lead a research project involving a group of researchers . The applicant becomes the project s PI and is responsible for developing the research programme, selecting researchers to participate, organising workshops and leading the group s research activities during the residential period at CAS. This structure is intended to give young researchers practical experience in research leadership while also helping them expand their international academic networks. CAS describes its broader mission as supporting excellent, curiosity-driven, blue-sky research. Its Young CAS programme specifically provides talented young scholars with facilities and uninterrupted time for research. How Much Funding Does the Young CAS Grant Provide? Each successful Young CAS project receives up to NOK 750,000 over the two-year programme period . The funding is divided broadly into two components: 1. Workshop funding Up to NOK 250,000 is available for organising three intensive workshops. These workshops form an important part of the collaborative structure of the programme and are intended to bring researchers together to develop the project s research objectives. 2. Research-stay funding Up to NOK 500,000 is available for the two-month research stay at CAS. The funding can cover eligible costs associated with the gatherings and research stay, including: Travel Accommodation Food expenses Documentable teaching replacement costs for participating fellows The grant is therefore structured around activities that allow researchers to meet, collaborate and spend dedicated time developing the project rather than simply providing unrestricted individual research funding. What Does the Two-Year Programme Involve? The Young CAS Grant runs from August 2027 through June 2029 and is organised across two academic years. Year One: August 2027 to June 2028 During the first year, the PI will organise two workshops: One workshop at CAS in Oslo. One workshop at the PI s home institution. Holding one workshop at the home institution allows the researcher to maintain connections with their existing research environment while also bringing the Young CAS project into the wider academic community. Year Two: August 2028 to June 2029 During the second year, the research group will gather at CAS for a two-month research stay . The third and final workshop will also take place at CAS. There is also an opportunity to host one day and dinner at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters. The PI is expected to lead the group throughout the entire two-month residential research period. What Support Does CAS Provide? The Young CAS Grant provides more than financial support. Throughout the project period, CAS provides assistance designed to make the research activities possible. Successful projects receive: Assistance with planning and organising the three workshops Office facilities for the research stay Four well-equipped office spaces allocated to each Young CAS project Seminar rooms equipped for meetings and video conferencing IT services Library services Accommodation within walking distance of CAS for researchers who are not based in the Oslo area Accessible facilities, including ramps and elevators The programme is specifically designed around group-based research. CAS recommends that at least three of the four designated office spaces should be used consistently during the research stay. Who Can Apply for the Young CAS Grant? The eligibility requirements are specific. Applicants must satisfy the following main conditions: Completed PhD The applicant must have completed a PhD by the application deadline. Age requirement The applicant must be below 40 years of age at the application deadline . CAS provides extensions to the age limit for certain circumstances, including: Statutory leaves of absence Compulsory military or civilian service Continuous full-time and/or part-time sick leave amounting to at least eight weeks of full-time absence There is no age limit for the other researchers participating in the project . Full-time academic employment Applicants must hold a full-time academic position at one of CAS s partner institutions at the application deadline and throughout the project period. The position does not necessarily have to be permanent. Researchers may also change their affiliation between CAS partner institutions, subject to the programme requirements. Support from the home institution The application must be supported by the applicant s head of department . The supporting institution must confirm, among other things, that the researcher will retain their salary and be released from other obligations during periods when they are undertaking activities associated with the Young CAS Grant. Temporary academic positions Researchers employed on temporary contracts can also qualify. However, their employment contract must cover at least the first year of the programme . Applicants whose employment situation for the second year is uncertain may still apply. Continued participation in the second year would require re-employment at one of CAS s partner institutions and a new letter of support submitted at least two months before the second year begins. Do Applicants Need Previous Project Leadership Experience? Previous project leadership experience is preferred but not mandatory . This is significant because the programme itself is intended to help young researchers gain experience as research leaders. The successful PI will gain practical experience in: Developing a collaborative research programme Selecting and coordinating researchers Organising international workshops Managing research activities Leading a residential research group Building international academic connections Developing a research project toward future funding opportunities What Kind of Research Projects Does CAS Accept? The proposed project must fit the broader mission of CAS. Young CAS projects should focus on excellent basic and curiosity-driven research . Applicants are encouraged to propose research that: Challenges established assumptions or given truths Addresses significant research questions Has the potential to advance the research frontier Has a strong theoretical or conceptual foundation Can benefit from collaborative international research Can make effective use of the workshops and residential research period Researchers from all academic disciplines are encouraged to apply . However, applicants should understand the nature of the CAS facilities and programme. Laboratory-based research cannot be conducted at CAS itself. Projects involving laboratory work, fieldwork or data collection may still apply if the Young CAS project is intended to develop the theoretical aspects of the research. Can Laboratory or Field Research Projects Apply? Yes, but there is an important limitation. CAS does not provide facilities for conducting laboratory-based research during the residential stay. Projects involving: Laboratory work Fieldwork Data collection may still be considered where these activities support a broader project focused on theoretical research. Applicants therefore need to design the project around what can realistically be accomplished during the CAS residency. International Collaboration Is an Important Part of the Programme The Young CAS Grant is structured to encourage researchers to build an international research group. Applicants must provide a list of 3–6 researchers whom they intend to invite as fellows. The proposed participants should preferably include researchers from outside the applicant s home institution and/or researchers based abroad. CAS also recommends inviting fellows who can participate actively in the workshops and remain at CAS throughout the two-month research stay. The application should explain why the proposed group has been assembled and how each researcher s expertise contributes to the feasibility of the project. What Documents Are Required? Applicants need to prepare several documents before submitting their application. 1. Project description The project description can be no more than four pages , excluding references. The document must begin with approximately 400 words written for readers outside the applicant s specific research field . The remainder can address specialists in the relevant field. The project description should cover: The hypotheses and/or research questions The project s purpose and objectives How the project fits CAS s mission The theoretical framework The methodology The most important existing research in the area The project s contribution to the research frontier Expected outcomes during and after the grant period The added value of participating in the Young CAS Grant Programme The references are limited to one page . 2. Project activity plan Applicants must submit a one-page implementation plan explaining how the activities will be organised during the programme. The plan should demonstrate how the applicant will: Lead the project Achieve its research objectives Organise the workshops Use the research stay Coordinate the different project activities 3. List of proposed researchers Applicants must provide a list of 3–6 researchers they plan to invite. The list should include: Academic title Area or areas of expertise Institutional affiliation Explanation of why the group has been composed in that way Explanation of how the participants contribute to the feasibility of the project Letters of intent from proposed participants are not required . 4. Budget Applicants must submit a budget draft accompanied by the necessary explanations of expenses. CAS provides a budget template for applicants. 5. Ethical self-assessment A brief ethical self-assessment of no more than half a page is required. The applicant must certify that they are familiar with the relevant ethical guidelines. 6. CV and publication list Applicants must provide a CV containing a publication list. The CV should be no more than four pages in total and should use the required template. 7. Letter of support A letter of support is required from the head of the relevant section at the applicant s home institution. The letter must cover the August 2027–June 2029 period and explain: How the grant will support the applicant s career opportunities How the project will benefit the department or institute The applicant s employment period if they hold a temporary position Confirmation that the applicant will retain their salary Confirmation that the applicant will be exempt from other obligations during periods of Young CAS Grant activities Confirmation that the home institution will host the second gathering during the first year What About Research Ethics and Regulatory Approval? Applicants whose research requires approval from a relevant authority need to account for this in their application. Depending on the nature of the research, this could include approval from: The Norwegian Data Protection Authority Regional Committees for Medical and Health Research Ethics Another appropriate regulatory or ethical body Where pre-approval is required, applicants must confirm that the necessary approval will be obtained before the project begins. How Will Applications Be Evaluated? Applications will be assessed by a panel of generalists . This makes the requirement for a clear opening explanation particularly relevant. Applicants need to make the project understandable beyond their narrow research speciality. The selection process considers: Scientific quality The applicant s academic merits Alignment between the proposed project and CAS s mission Compliance with the formal requirements of the call A selection committee involving representatives from CAS, the CAS Board of Directors and the Young Academy of Norway will prepare a shortlist. The CAS Board of Directors will ultimately select the two Young CAS Grant projects . The selection decision is expected in February 2027 . What Should Applicants Pay Attention to When Preparing Their Proposal? A strong application needs to do more than describe an interesting research topic. The proposal should show why the Young CAS structure is particularly useful for achieving the project s objectives. Applicants should therefore clearly connect: Research question → research team → workshops → residential stay → expected outcomes → career development The application should make it easy for evaluators to understand: What problem the project addresses. Why the problem deserves further investigation. What the proposed research group will contribute. Why an international and collaborative approach is appropriate. What will be achieved during the two-year period. Why the CAS environment is useful to the project. How participation will strengthen the applicant s development as a research leader. CAS specifically asks applicants to explain how the programme s gatherings, research stay and networking opportunities will contribute to achieving the research objectives and advancing the applicant s career. What Happens During the Two-Month Research Stay? The residential component is one of the defining features of the Young CAS Grant. The PI is expected to be present and lead the group throughout the full two-month stay. CAS expects the project to function as a collaborative research environment rather than a situation where the PI works independently at the Centre. Researchers who stay for four weeks or more, including the PI, are considered fellows. Researchers who stay for less than four weeks may participate as affiliated researchers when office space permits. Important Programme Scheduling Information Applicants should also take CAS s annual closure periods into account when planning workshops and the residential research period. CAS is closed: Between 1 July and 14 August During Easter week During the week between Christmas and New Year s Day, when administrative support is unavailable These dates should be considered when preparing the implementation plan. Can the Grant Be Used to Write Other Funding Applications? The workshops and residential research stay should not be used primarily for writing applications . However, CAS says it is an advantage if the project can be developed with the possibility of seeking future support from other research funding organisations. Examples mentioned by CAS include the Research Council of Norway and the European Research Council (ERC) . This means applicants can demonstrate how the Young CAS project may form the foundation for future research development without making grant-writing the central purpose of the programme. How to Apply for the Young CAS Grant Applications must be submitted electronically through the UNIFOR application system . All required documents must: Be written in English Be prepared according to the relevant templates where applicable Be saved as PDF files Be uploaded through the electronic application system Be submitted before the deadline The application system closes after the deadline, and late applications cannot be processed. The deadline is: 19 November 2026 at 23:59 Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final hours to upload their documents. Click HERE for application. Young CAS Grant Deadline The application deadline for the Young CAS Grant 2027–2029 is 19 November 2026 at 23:59 . Applicants should ensure that their complete application has been submitted electronically before the UNIFOR system closes. Late submissions cannot be processed. Why This Opportunity May Be Relevant to Early-Career Researchers The Young CAS Grant combines several elements that are often difficult for researchers to access at the beginning of an academic career. Instead of focusing only on individual research funding, the programme gives the selected researcher an opportunity to develop as a research leader and project organiser . The successful PI will have to coordinate researchers, organise workshops, manage a research programme and lead a residential research group. The programme also creates an environment in which researchers from different institutions and countries can work together around a common research question. For researchers who already have a clear research direction and meet the PhD, age and employment requirements, the programme provides a structured way to develop an international collaborative project. Important Eligibility Reminder for International Applicants The Young CAS Grant should not be confused with an unrestricted international scholarship open to anyone worldwide. Although CAS encourages researchers from all academic disciplines , applicants must meet the programme s employment requirement: they must hold a full-time academic position at one of CAS s partner institutions at the relevant time. Therefore, nationality or country of residence alone does not determine eligibility. An applicant from outside Norway may qualify if they meet the stated requirements, including the requirement concerning a full-time position at a CAS partner institution. Conversely, being from an eligible country does not by itself make someone eligible if they do not satisfy the institutional employment requirement. Final Thoughts The Young CAS Grant 2027–2029 is structured as a research leadership opportunity for early-career academics who have completed a PhD and are ready to develop a collaborative research project. The selected researchers will not simply receive funding for individual research. They will lead a research group, organise three workshops, bring together researchers with complementary expertise and spend two months conducting collaborative research at the Centre for Advanced Study in Oslo. CAS will select two projects , with each receiving up to NOK 750,000 over the two-year programme period, together with research facilities and administrative support. Researchers interested in applying should pay close attention to the eligibility conditions, particularly the under-40 age requirement, completed PhD, full-time academic position at a CAS partner institution and institutional letter of support . title: University of Luxembourg YADIAS Doctoral Fellowship 2027: Fully Funded 4-Year PhD Opportunity for International Students
summary: The University of Luxembourg YADIAS Doctoral Fellowship 2027 is now open to qualified researchers interested in pursuing a doctoral degree through an international, interdisciplinary and research-focused programme in Luxembourg. The Young Academics Doctoral Fellows IAS (YADIAS) programme will recruit 15 full-time international doctoral candidates for a 48-month programme beginning in June 2027. Supported through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) COFUND initiative under Horizon Europe , the YADIAS programme combines doctoral research with structured career development, international networking and interdisciplinary training. Selected fellows will receive an indicative gross living allowance of €3,841 per month , paid 12 times a year. One of the programme’s most distinctive features is its bottom-up approach. Rather than requiring applicants to select from a fixed list of doctoral research projects, YADIAS allows candidates to develop their own research topics within the disciplines available at the University of Luxembourg and identify suitable principal and co-supervisors. Applications are open until 30 November 2026 at 02:00 UTC . About the University of Luxembourg YADIAS Doctoral Fellowship The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a strong focus on multilingualism, interdisciplinarity and international collaboration. Its research community includes staff from more than 90 countries and maintains partnerships with European institutions, companies, government bodies, NGOs and other organisations. The YADIAS programme is hosted by the university’s Institute for Advanced Studies (IAS) , which was established in 2020 to strengthen interdisciplinary research and attract international research talent. The institute focuses on four broad objectives: Supporting bold and interdisciplinary research at the forefront of science. Promoting excellence, interdisciplinarity and internationality. Connecting the University of Luxembourg with international researchers and the wider public. Helping attract and retain international research talent. Through YADIAS, the university is extending this mission to early-stage researchers who want to pursue doctoral studies in an internationally connected research environment. What Does the YADIAS Programme Offer? YADIAS is a 48-month doctoral research and career development programme designed for 15 international doctoral candidates. The programme goes beyond conventional doctoral training by combining individual research with interdisciplinary, international and intersectoral development. Selected fellows will have the opportunity to: Conduct a four-year doctoral research project. Develop a research topic based on their own academic interests. Choose a principal supervisor and co-supervisor. Work across disciplinary boundaries. Develop advanced expertise in their main research field. Expand their knowledge of other academic disciplines. Build international research networks. Strengthen their employability and transferable skills. Prepare for future academic or non-academic research careers. Work toward the award of a doctoral degree. The programme is particularly suitable for researchers who already have a clear research direction but want the academic freedom and international environment to develop that idea further. A Bottom-Up Approach to Doctoral Research A major advantage of the YADIAS programme is its bottom-up research model . In many doctoral programmes, candidates apply to a predefined research project developed by a professor or research group. YADIAS takes a different approach. Candidates are given the opportunity to propose their own research topic, provided that the proposed research fits within the disciplines available at the University of Luxembourg. Applicants can also identify their preferred principal and co-supervisors. This approach gives prospective fellows greater ownership of their doctoral research from the beginning. It also encourages researchers to develop projects that bring together different academic perspectives. For candidates whose research interests do not fit neatly into one discipline, this interdisciplinary structure may be particularly relevant. Available Research Fields The YADIAS Doctoral Fellowship is open across a broad range of research areas. The advertised opportunity lists fields including: Educational sciences Architecture Biological sciences Chemistry Cultural studies Economics Engineering Geography Environmental science History Juridical sciences Literature Management sciences Sociology Mathematics Medical sciences Physics The broad disciplinary scope means applicants from different academic backgrounds can potentially develop research projects within the programme. However, applicants should ensure that their proposed project fits the University of Luxembourg’s available academic expertise and that suitable supervision can be established. Who Can Apply for the YADIAS Doctoral Fellowship? The programme is intended for international doctoral candidates who meet the academic and language requirements for doctoral admission at the University of Luxembourg. Academic requirement Applicants must hold a: Master’s degree or equivalent qualification. The position is classified as a First Stage Researcher (R1) opportunity, corresponding to researchers at the early stage of their research careers. A relevant academic background is expected because applicants must develop a viable doctoral research project within one of the university’s available disciplines. Language requirement Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis . For applicants whose doctoral research will be conducted in English, this means they should be prepared to demonstrate the required level of English proficiency through the accepted documentation or certificates specified by the University of Luxembourg. Applicants should consult the university’s doctoral admission requirements for details concerning accepted language certificates. International Mobility and Research Environment YADIAS is based on incoming mobility , making it particularly relevant to researchers who want to pursue their doctoral studies in Luxembourg as part of an international research career. The University of Luxembourg offers a highly international environment, with researchers and staff from more than 90 countries. Fellows will also be part of a research ecosystem connected to a variety of organisations, including: European institutions Innovative companies The Luxembourg financial centre Ministries Local governments NGOs Associations Other professional and non-academic organisations These connections are important because YADIAS is designed not only to develop academic expertise but also to expose researchers to professional environments beyond the university. Interdisciplinary and Career Development Training YADIAS places strong emphasis on preparing doctoral candidates for careers both inside and outside academia. During the programme, fellows will deepen their knowledge within their main discipline while developing broader interdisciplinary skills. The programme is also intended to improve: Research expertise Interdisciplinary collaboration International networking Employability Career planning Preparation for postdoctoral funding Transition into careers beyond academia This makes YADIAS more than a doctoral funding opportunity. It is structured as a broader research training and career development programme . The ultimate goal is to help fellows build the scientific and professional skills needed for advanced research careers. Fellowship Funding and Employment Conditions Successful candidates will receive a competitive contract and research conditions from the University of Luxembourg. The advertised indicative gross living allowance is €3,841 per month at the start of the project. The allowance is based on a full-time equivalent position and is paid 12 times per year . That corresponds to an indicative gross annual amount of approximately €46,092 before applicable deductions. The position is: Full-time 40 hours per week Temporary contract Four-year duration Expected to begin on 1 June 2027 Applicants should remember that the €3,841 figure is a gross amount, meaning the amount actually received after applicable deductions may be lower. How the YADIAS Selection Process Works The University of Luxembourg states that its YADIAS recruitment follows the principles of Open, Transparent and Merit-Based Recruitment (OTM-R) . Selection decisions are based on international peer review. An important part of the process is matching candidates with appropriate supervisors. The university specifically warns that the matchmaking stage can take considerable time . Applicants are therefore strongly encouraged to begin preparing their application well before the deadline. This is particularly important for candidates proposing their own research projects because they need enough time to identify suitable academic supervisors and develop a strong research proposal. How to Apply for the University of Luxembourg YADIAS Fellowship Interested candidates should follow these steps when preparing their application. 1. Review the YADIAS programme Begin by reviewing the official YADIAS information and determining whether your academic background and research interests fit the programme. Pay particular attention to the available research disciplines and doctoral admission requirements. 2. Develop your research idea Since YADIAS uses a bottom-up model, applicants should develop a clear research idea rather than waiting to select from a list of predetermined projects. Your research idea should be academically sound and relevant to one or more of the disciplines supported by the University of Luxembourg. If your topic crosses multiple disciplines, explain how the different areas contribute to the research problem. 3. Identify potential supervisors Applicants should consider potential principal and co-supervisors whose expertise matches their proposed research. Do not leave this step until the final days before the deadline because supervisor matchmaking can take considerable time. 4. Prepare the required documents Applicants should consult the official YADIAS application documents and templates to determine exactly what must be submitted. The programme provides dedicated documents and templates through its official website. 5. Submit through the correct application portal This is particularly important. The University of Luxembourg states that applications must be submitted exclusively through the dedicated YADIAS application link . Applications submitted through the general “Apply” button associated with the vacancy will not be reviewed or forwarded .
